analysis.title: DeskTalk - Democrats lead early, markets on the move
key_insights: Early election results favor Democrats: AP has called 21 House seats for Democrats vs 10 for Republicans, plus Senate seats in Virginia, Rhode Island, New Jersey, Delaware, Georgia, Illinois and Massachusetts.
Initial market reaction is risk-off. Equity futures, US yields and the dollar are lower. Tech stocks and Asian equities are under pressure, with Nasdaq futures down 0.5% and the Nikkei down 2%.
The 10y UST yield fell as much as 5bps to 4.91%.
In FX, activity is subdued on Citi's Asia eTrading desk. JPY and CHF outperformed early, with some of those gains pared back.
Citi strategists expect the Treasury to reduce issuance sizes in the 20-year and 30-year sectors at Wednesday's Quarterly Refunding Announcement (08:30 EST).
Prediction markets price the House at 98% and Senate control at 92% for Democrats.
Oil is trading lower after President Trump told the Financial Times the US has 'no immediate plan' to strike Iran.

sector_views.rationale: Tech stocks are under clear pressure in the initial risk-off reaction, with Nasdaq futures down 0.5%. This is market color, not a Citi sector call.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Fell as much as 5bps on early Democratic election results.
Citi strategists expect the Treasury to cut issuance in the 20-year and 30-year sectors.

trade_ideas.description: Watch Citi's 'Blue Sweep' basket (CGUSBLUW) if current election results continue to hold.
trade_ideas.rationale: Early results favor Democrats, with prediction markets pricing a strong night for them.

risk_factors: Election results are still coming in and could change from the early reads.
Further risk-off in tech and Asian equities if Democratic results continue.
